title: Harness of Minervini v2 doctrine.list response

examples: scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline doctrine list --context prospective_entry --family risk. --layer canonical

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

context.description: Exact analysis context, such as prospective_entry, active_position, setup, or market_analysis.

family.description: Claim ID prefix, such as risk. or setup.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

layer.description: Exact doctrine layer: canonical, practice, or harness.

limitations: Filters intersect; an unknown context, prefix, or layer returns an empty complete list.
Quarantined and out-of-scope records are excluded; doctrine show remains the audit accessor for a known ID.
Computability distinguishes deterministic measurements from claims requiring analyst judgment; inclusion is not an investment verdict.
--as-of stamps the envelope; doctrine content is versioned with the repository rather than market time.
x-capability-contract.output: Runtime claim rows with id, title, kind, layer, computability, registered threshold roles, and consumers. Use doctrine show with a returned ID for its full rule and source quotations.

status_meanings.needs_input: A filter is not a non-empty string or the as-of session is invalid.
status_meanings.ok: Matching runtime claims, or a legitimate empty list, were returned.

x-capability-contract.summary: Discover runtime doctrine claims and how each is read or measured.
